children: it continued to sign new compute capacity contracts at higher prices since June 30, 2026, including short-term agreements in the third quarter.

In the third quarter of 2026, the company has signed customer contracts with terms of roughly three to six months at pricing of about $40M per megawatt, based on annualized revenue relative to the power required to serve the related clusters.
CoreWeave also reiterated that it added more than $25B in net new customer commitments early in the third quarter, which were not included in its June 30 revenue backlog.
Total contracted power increased to about 4.2 gigawatts as of Aug. 11, from approximately 3.7 GW at June 30.
CRWV shares were up 1.6% premarket. The company separately
an at-the-market offering program to sell up to 35M shares of Class A common stock.

title: CoreWeave contracts new compute capacity at higher prices in Q3
